endorsements.quote: Model development processes must also emphasize fairness by ensuring diversity in data collection and by stratifying performance reporting according to population characteristics during validation and deployment phases.

At the same time, adherence to TRIPOD+AI and PROBAST+AI should be treated as a methodological expectation, not an optional add-on, because transparency and structured bias appraisal are necessary for evaluating whether apparently strong models are actually fit for clinical use ( 9 , 10 ).

Where feasible, model comparison should therefore extend beyond AUC to include calibration, subgroup error distribution, and decision-curve-oriented evaluation of clinical usefulness ( 9 , 10 , 16 , 17 ).

Model development processes must also emphasize fairness by ensuring diversity in data collection and by stratifying performance reporting according to population characteristics during validation and deployment phases.

unlisted_practices: Prioritize external validation of AI prediction models before claiming readiness for clinical use.
Locally recalibrate risk prediction models using local data before applying them to new populations.
Conduct multicenter studies in high-burden regions to develop locally adaptive prediction models.
Quantify whether added biomarkers improve discrimination, calibration, and net clinical benefit beyond baseline clinical models before including them.
Avoid treating Asian populations as homogeneous when developing or extrapolating prediction models.

screen.reason: This is a commentary/perspective article arguing for clinical equity, external validation, and subgroup reporting when translating AI cardiovascular risk models to clinical practice.
